title: Internal inflammatory root resorption
topic: Necrotic infected coronal pulp + vital apical pulp let odontoclasts balloon the canal; root canal treatment stops it; 3 classic X-ray signs.

claims.claim: Internal resorption: necrotic (infected) pulp coronal, vital pulp apical to the lesion - the classic model (inflammatory type)
claims.source: Abbott PV, Lin S. Dent Traumatol 2022;38:267-85 (PMID 35605161) - review full text, sect. 5.2; definition: Patel S, Ricucci D, Durak C, Tay F. J Endod 2010;36:1107-21 (PMID 20630282) - abstract

claims.claim: Requirement 1: necrotic, infected pulp coronal to the lesion = the stimulus
claims.source: Abbott PV, Lin S. Dent Traumatol 2022;38:267-85 (PMID 35605161) - review full text, sect. 5.2

claims.claim: Requirement 2: vital pulp apical to the lesion = the blood supply
claims.source: Abbott PV, Lin S. Dent Traumatol 2022;38:267-85 (PMID 35605161) - review full text, sect. 5.2; Patel S, Saberi N, Pimental T, Teng PH. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full text

claims.claim: Predentin lost -> dentin exposed (entry for clastic cells)
claims.source: Patel et al. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full text

claims.claim: Odontoclasts (label); the canal balloons into a symmetric oval continuous with the canal (picture; schematic: cell number, size, route, mid-root site)
claims.source: Patel et al. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full text (odontoclasts; "symmetrical oval- or circular-shaped extension of the root canal"); Patel et al. J Endod 2010;36:1107-21 (PMID 20630282) - abstract (clastic destruction of dentin only, not the shape)

claims.claim: RCT: pulp out -> blood supply cut -> resorption stops (defect stays; schematic of root canal treatment; expert consensus, no trial)
claims.source: Patel S et al. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full text; Nilsson E et al. Int J Dent 2013;2013:929486 (PMID 24348560) - abstract

claims.claim: CBCT: perforated? Calcium silicate cement (e.g. MTA) in the defect and the perforation (case-report level; the picture also shows an unlabeled gutta-percha fill apical to it)

Int Endod J 2009;42:831-8 (PMID 19627378) - abstract

claims.claim: Classic X-ray sign 1: symmetric, well-defined ballooning
claims.source: Patel et al. 2022 (PMID 35229320), after Gartner AH et al. J Endod 1976;2:329-34 (PMID 1069086; no abstract, not read); Aidos H, Diogo P, Santos JM. Eur Endod J 2018;3:134-45 (PMID 32161869); Thomas P et al. ISRN Dent 2014;2014:759326 (PMID 24944822) - review full texts

claims.claim: Classic X-ray sign 2: canal outline lost (inside the lesion)

claims.source: Aidos et al. 2018 (PMID 32161869; after Kanas & Kanas 2011, not read); Patel et al. 2022 (PMID 35229320); Thomas et al. 2014 (PMID 24944822) - review full texts

caption:
Internal (inflammatory) resorption: the canal wall is resorbed from the inside.
Classic model: necrotic, infected coronal pulp = stimulus; vital apical pulp = blood supply; odontoclasts work where predentin is lost. Root canal treatment removes both, so it stops; lost dentin is not restored. Classic 2-D signs are fallible: internal and external cervical resorption can look alike. CBCT shows perforation. Rare replacement type: irregular, mottled. Evidence: reviews, case reports.
Schematic animation.
Refs: Patel 2022, Patel 2009 Int Endod J; Abbott & Lin 2022 Dent Traumatol; Patel 2010 J Endod; Aidos 2018 Eur Endod J
